text.p: The following are the main stories in Lithuania's newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The winner of the parliamentary elections Vytautas Landsbergis tries to get rid of his anti-Russian image at a conference on Lithuanian-Russian relations over the weekend.
- Vandals struck again in the second city of Kaunas when the walls of three churches were daubed with anti-Church graffitti.
- Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas meets the leaders of five political parties who got into parliament after the elections.
- Russian oil giant Lukoil has decided not to subscribe to the third issue of shares in the planned Butinge Nafta oil terminal as it was not satisfied with the schedule of financing.
- Some 278 students reached a world record for filling a bus with people in Kaunas and travelling one kilometre.

- The central electoral committee announced official parliamentary results on Sunday after the second round of elections on October 20. The Homeland Union won 70 seats, the Christian Democrats 16, the Centre Union 13 and the Lithuanian Democratic Labour Party (LDLP) got 12 seats in the 141-seat parliament. Eight other parties won one seat and there are four independents.
- Belarussian customs officials confiscated on Friday night the whole 200,000 print run of the Belarus opposition newspaper Nasa Niva, which is printed in Lithuania.
